sampling_model.design: The certificate-independent structural input fixes the legal action catalogue and costs and supplies the explicitly charged source oracle. Each selected protocol runs independently on fresh units; a distinct protocol is charged once, its law handle and exact support table are returned once, and all positive labelled slices are reusable.
sampling_model.units: Each SELECT draws a fresh independent unit from the target population, and all potential responses for that unit are generated by one recursive finite-discrete SCM compatible with \(G\).
sampling_model.treatment: RAND actions replace a node mechanism for all affected children, while CTF-RAND actions fix the value delivered to their catalogued child subset without erasing the unit's natural decision.
sampling_model.overlap: For a legal protocol \(S\), positivity is required exactly for each used event \(H_{\mathrm{slice}}(S,\ell)\), and is decided from the exact support bit table returned by \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}(S)\). Events with unrecorded endpoints, uncatalogued assignments, conflicting values, or zero support are inadmissible; unused cells are unrestricted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None is required for the symbolic theorem. The source oracle returns an opaque complete-law handle and exact finite support, and every query and answer bit is charged; scalar-functional evaluation and empirical law estimation remain outside scope.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Algorithm 2 and Theorem 3.5 decide an unnested counterfactual query from a fixed finite collection of supplied input distributions.
A Layer-3 distribution is realizable if and only if CTF-REALIZE returns a sample.
Theorem 1 gives singleton reduction for a connected ordinary target, Lemma 3 characterizes singleton feasibility by hedge hitting, and Theorem 2 proves NP-hardness.

Theorem 1 and Lemma 3 reduce a c-component ordinary target to one minimum-weight hedge-hitting intervention, Lemma 7 certifies exact Algorithm 2, and Proposition 3 certifies exact Algorithm 3 for a general target.
Ordinary minimum-cost proxy experiment design admits weighted Max-SAT and integer-programming formulations.
The ctfID algorithm is complete for counterfactual identification from arbitrary observational and experimental distributions.
Under positivity, generalized identification reduces to a series of classical identification subproblems.
The algorithm returns all and only representative counterfactual possibly-optimal minimal intervention sets.

body.tldr: A finite physical catalogue can contain many legal Layer-2.5 acquisitions, but a computational claim must expose the source laws and exact support tests. The instance is therefore a certificate-independent structural string paired with a precisely charged oracle returning one immutable complete-law handle and finite support table per queried protocol. Operational acceptance performs every positivity test from that table and runs complete CTFIDU\({}^{+}\). The load-bearing theorem places one selected source and restriction schema outside all assignment and equality-type branches of each target district, giving at most \(k\) source-slice records and a polynomial certificate bound. This yields an exact, explicitly exponential minimum-cost optimizer and infeasibility decision, a static fixed-factor obstruction, a two-way ordinary \(Q[S]\) embedding, and a positive binary cost-one-versus-two CTF-RAND separation. The sharp complexity of searching an unrestricted source oracle is the first-class open question; bounded-treewidth compilation is not claimed.

project_justification.gap: Complete counterfactual identification fixes its source collection in advance, physical realizability treats one source law at a time, and Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025) optimize ordinary intervention objects under fixed \(Q[S]\) source-family semantics. None supplies an operational cost problem that charges source-law and support access or resolves assignment-sensitive source switching.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a certificate-independent physical interface with explicit source support, a uniform factorwise acceptance witness, and an exact cost frontier whose computational accounting includes every source-oracle reply.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a charged source oracle, operational complete-run acceptance, a uniform one-source-per-factor theorem and polynomial certificate bound, exact finite optimization with an infeasibility alternative, a fixed-factor obstruction, an exact ordinary-source embedding, and a fully specified positive physical separation.

body.related_work: Raghavan and Bareinboim (2025) define SELECT, RAND, CTF-RAND, and READ and prove CTF-REALIZE complete for physical sampling; their result determines realizability, not a minimum-cost collection or a charged source-support interface. Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026) prove CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) complete for a fixed collection of Layer-3 inputs; Algorithm 2 and Appendix E motivate the uniform-normalization proof but do not exchange source choice across value assignments and equality types. Correa, Lee, and Bareinboim (2021) provide unnesting and ctf-factorization from fixed sources. Kivva et al. (2022) establish positivity-sensitive generalized identification, while the exact event-level slice positivity here is a novel physical input restriction and is checked only through the explicit support oracle. Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (2025), Theorem 1 on page 5, reduce a c-component target to one ordinary intervention; Lemma 3 on page 8 gives its minimum-weight hedge-hitting formulation; Theorems 2 and 3 on pages 6--7 and Corollaries 1 and 2 on pages 7--8 establish NP-completeness and logarithmic inapproximability; Lemma 7 on page 12 certifies exact Algorithm 2; and Proposition 3 on page 16 certifies exact Algorithm 3 for a general target. The ordinary-subclass theorem matches that ordinary \(Q[S]\) object and fixed source-family semantics exactly. The general physical object instead permits edge-specific CTF-RAND actions, READ-dependent slices, and cost reuse, and proves a compact uniform factor certificate, while computational optimization remains finite exhaustive under the charged oracle. The familiar \(H_k\) guarantee is retained solely as the already-known weighted-cover corollary under three explicitly novel restricted-subclass conditions. Elahi et al. (2024) accelerate ordinary proxy experiment design without physical counterfactual actions. Courcelle and Mosbah (1993) and Arnborg, Lagergren, and Seese (1991) require a finite local relational predicate; an arbitrary source-support oracle is not silently treated as such, so no bounded-treewidth compiler or fixed-parameter runtime is claimed. Park and Lee (2026) supply the downstream counterfactual bandit setting, not an acquisition-cost theorem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform source-choice theorem is the load-bearing target: failure on any finite assignment or equality pattern falsifies the polynomial certificate and exact optimizer as stated. The source oracle may return exponentially long support tables, all charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\), and exhaustive certificate search remains exponential in \(B_{\mathrm{cert}}\). A bounded-treewidth compiler requires a separately justified local representation of oracle answers and lies outside the claimed kernel. The measured-ancestry rule rejects \(\operatorname{READ}(Y)\) alone for natural \(X\to Y\) whenever \(X\) is required, and rejects any unrecorded required natural parent or mediator. Physical slice positivity rejects exactly a used RAND, CTF-RAND, and ancestral READ conjunction having zero support.
body.honest_scope: The uniform one-source-per-factor equivalence, its canonical certificate bound, and the exact oracle-backed cost frontier are theorem targets; the oracle-query complexity frontier is open. Measured ancestry and positive admissible source events are novel physical restrictions. The source interface makes every law handle, support table, positivity decision, query, and answer explicit and charged. The one-action, protocolwise-legality, and factorwise-no-synergy conditions are novel restricted-subclass assumptions justified by isolated single-assay platforms; they are not attributed to ordinary design theory. The project claims neither a full-incidence compiler nor a treewidth bound, a scalar identifying-functional output, efficient numerical evaluation, compactness, conditional-query completeness, arbitrary partial-read completeness, mediator-depth fixed-parameter tractability, polynomial lower certificates, nor a global approximation ratio. General identifying expressions, support tables, search traces, and infeasibility certificates may be exponential.
